page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, providing a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core mapping with 1.0 thread per core. It includes 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it lacks GPU acceleration. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the ecs.sn2.xlarge demonstrates modest performance characteristics. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests via stress-ng and Geekbench place the instance in the bottom 25% and bottom 10% categories, reflecting its older hardware generation. Memory bandwidth tests show weak read-only performance for both small and large blocks, though large-block write bandwidth reaches average levels. Passmark CPU and extended instruction tests also score in the average range, indicating stable execution for standard instruction sets. However, database operations, Redis SET performance, and static web serving throughput remain in the lower 25% tier.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn2.xlarge offers a predictable, dedicated resource profile without the premium associated with high-performance compute or memory-optimized classes. The lack of bundled local storage and moderate network baseline suggests it is best suited for workloads that do not demand high IOPS or rapid data transfer. Appropriate workloads include general-purpose applications, small-scale web serving, light database tasks, and basic development or testing environments where dedicated CPU allocation is preferred over shared-core burstable instances.
